title: An HTTP server sends responses
summary: Apache HTTP Server accepts web requests and sends responses. For a static site, the response body often comes straight from a file.
introduction: Apache HTTP Server accepts web requests and sends responses. For a static site, the response body often comes straight from a file. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain an http server sends responses
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Apache HTTP Server accepts web requests and sends responses. For a static site, the response body often comes straight from a file.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.text: Read these examples as configuration fragments. Commands require a separate authorised local Apache installation. No server is added to the learning application.
This course teaches the basics. It does not cover every feature of Apache HTTP Server. Keep real personal data and secret keys out of practice files.

blocks.code:
Request: GET /club.html
Response status: 200 if the file is served
Response body: the HTML file
blocks.title: An HTTP server sends responses

blocks.text: The browser displays the returned HTML. A web server is separate from the browser that runs the page scripts.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Draw the path from a browser request to a static file.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Apache HTTP Server is not the same project as every other tool with Apache in its name.
For more detail later, use this [Apache HTTP Server further reading](https://httpd.apache.org/docs/2.4/getting-started.html).
